decisions.reason: As a close-to-core service offer, the fifteen-day express delivery program fits the firm's existing production, logistics, and service capabilities, so management is more likely to improve it than remove it.

The seventy-two-hour express delivery program is still related to the core business, but its demanding promise and likely overlap with other express offers make it more exposed to withdrawal than the other launches.
The fire-resistant steel exterior door sits directly in the firm's established technical and regulatory knowledge base, and its prominent launch and approval indicate a strong case for retention.

The express delivery program for doors and gates extends the established one-stop offer and can be learned and optimized within the firm's existing capabilities, though future consolidation remains possible.

The online ordering and digital services platform builds on the established offer and supports the firm's strategic move toward deeper service and advisory support, so it is likely to be developed further rather than dropped.
The fire and smoke protection door is highly related to the firm's existing safety, compliance, and door-system expertise, which makes continued commercialization likely.
